settings.heading: America’s Most Overlooked Childhood Threat
settings.alt: News headlines and studies about parasites in children, with kids playing in mulch, with a dog and at a school water fountain
settings.text:
Your child isn’t “just being a kid.” Something’s off, and you can feel it.

  • The meltdowns that come out of nowhere.
  • The constant hunt for sugar and carbs.
  • The tossing and turning at night.
  • The “my tummy hurts” that never quite goes away.
  • That nagging sense that your kid just isn’t themselves.

Everyone tells you it’s a phase. That all kids go through it.

But when the signs keep stacking up, nothing you try seems to help, and no one can tell you why, it’s worth asking a different question:

What if it starts in the gut?

Your child’s gut does far more than digest food. It plays a central role in their immunity, their energy, and even their mood. And one of the most overlooked things that can quietly disrupt it? Parasites.
settings.stat: CDC: Pinworms are the #1 worm infection in the U.S., and kids are the most affected
settings.stat_note: ⚠️ And they spread easily through schools, daycares, and entire households
settings.warn: Left unchecked, chronic gut parasites can rob a growing body of the nutrients it needs, during the exact years your child’s brain and body are still being built.
settings.good: But when you break the cycle and restore their gut, you give your child the best chance to be their happy, healthy self again.
settings.accordions:
🤔 Why hasn’t my pediatrician mentioned this? |

The CDC classifies parasites in America as officially “neglected”: overlooked, underdiagnosed, and undertreated. (Source: CDC, 2010)

In fact, over 60 million Americans are living with parasites - most without knowing.

Because most infections are only flagged when symptoms are severe: visible worms, heavy vomiting, serious diarrhea.

Low-grade infections that show up as mood changes, sleep issues, gut problems, and appetite changes look like dozens of other childhood conditions.

When doctors do test, the most common method (stool testing) misses parasites up to 70% of the time.

🦠 How do kids actually get parasites? |

Exposure is constant—and it’s not your child’s fault.

Parasite eggs are microscopic and survive 2-3 weeks on surfaces.

Kids are exposed through:

  • 🐾 Pets — Dogs and cats licking faces, hands, or sharing beds after being outside
  • 🍽️ Food — Unwashed produce, undercooked meat, or contaminated seafood (CDC estimates 48M foodborne illnesses annually)
  • 🏫 School — Shared bathrooms, playground equipment, and surfaces touched by infected children

The cycle:

  1. Kid touches contaminated surface
  2. One hand-to-mouth moment (eating, nail-biting)
  3. Eggs hatch within hours
  4. After 2-4 weeks, worms lay thousands more eggs at night
  5. Damage builds silently until symptoms appear
🔬 What are parasites actually doing inside my child’s body? |

While they go undetected, parasites are quietly doing three things:

  • Damaging the gut lining — the gut wall is what keeps harmful things contained. Parasites create gaps in it, letting toxins leak directly into the bloodstream and triggering reactions throughout the entire body.
  • Triggering constant inflammation — your child’s immune system goes into overdrive trying to fight it. That chronic low-grade inflammation is what drives the mood swings, sleep problems, irritability, skin issues, and rashes.
  • Stealing key nutrients — parasites feed on zinc, iron, and B12 before your child’s body can absorb them. These are what the brain uses to regulate mood, focus, and energy.
settings.text2: Despite how common they are, parasites are rarely the first thing parents think of, because the signs blend right into everyday childhood: restless nights, tummy aches, a kid who just isn’t themselves.
